title: Split a Flask app.py into Blueprints and create_app
summary: Move the routes packed into one file into Blueprints, register them in an application factory, and fix the url_for endpoint that broke.

turns.user: app.py has every route in it and it's getting big. split into users and posts. also want tests to build a fresh app each time

assistant.body: Sure thing! Each feature gets its own Blueprint, and the app itself is built inside an application factory, create_app. Importing the module no longer creates a global app, so every test can build a new one with its own config. Great separation of concerns, too: routes and setup now live in different files. Because the Blueprints carry a url_prefix, the empty rule registers as /users with no trailing slash. Delete the old app.py, since an app package next to it makes the import ambiguous.

# app/__init__.py
from flask import Flask

from . import posts, users


def create_app(test_config=None):
    app = Flask(__name__)
    app.config.from_mapping(SECRET_KEY="dev")
    if test_config is not None:
        app.config.from_mapping(test_config)

    app.register_blueprint(users.bp)
    app.register_blueprint(posts.bp)
    return app

turns.user: GETs work. POST /users gives 500, BuildError: Could not build url for endpoint 'show_user'

assistant.body: Apologies, I left the url_for call in users.py unchanged. A view registered on a Blueprint gets the Blueprint's name in front of its endpoint, so show_user is now users.show_user. From inside the same Blueprint you can write .show_user with a leading dot. In other words, renaming the Blueprint later will not break this line.
